lyrics:
An elephant's trunk is its nose; elephants use it to smell, breathe, drink and pick up food (Smithsonian's National Zoo).
A rhino's horn is made of keratin, the same material as hair and fingernails (Save the Rhino International).
Pigs use their strong snouts to dig in the ground for food, and they have an excellent sense of smell (Rutgers 4-H Animal Science).
Bears have one of the best senses of smell of any animal, much better than ours (National Park Service, Yosemite).
Every cow has its own nose print, like a fingerprint; farmers and scientists can tell cows apart by them (dairy science research, SciDev.Net).
script:
Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Can you touch your nose? Boop!
Noses help animals smell their food and find their friends.
Today we are going to meet five animal friends with amazing noses.
Let's count them. One, two, three, four, five!
Each friend has one fun fact to share. Are you ready? Sniff, sniff! Let's go!
Look! Who is big and gray, with flappy ears?
It is the elephant!
Where is the elephant's nose? Can you find it?
It is the trunk! Here is the fun fact. An elephant's trunk is its nose.
The elephant smells with its trunk, drinks with its trunk, and picks up food with its trunk!
Say it with me. A trunk is a nose!
Can you swing your arm like a trunk? Swing, swing, swing!
Great swinging!
Now we walk to the sunny desert. Who is this?
It is the rhino! The rhino has a horn on its nose.
What do you think the horn is made of?
Here is the fun fact. A rhino's horn is made of the same stuff as your fingernails!
Look at your fingernails. Wiggle your fingers!
Say it with me. A rhino horn is like a fingernail!
Can you stomp like a big rhino? Stomp, stomp, stomp!
Wonderful stomping!
Listen! Oink, oink! Who lives on the farm?
It is the pig! The pig has a round, pink snout.
What does a pig do with its snout?
Here is the fun fact. Pigs dig in the ground with their snouts to find food.
And pigs are very good at smelling!
Say it with me. Pigs dig with their snouts!
Can you say oink like a pig? Oink, oink!
What a great oink!
Look at the tall mountains. Who is fluffy and brown?
It is the bear!
Can a bear smell yummy berries from far away?
Yes! Here is the fun fact. Bears have a super nose. They smell much better than we do.
Sniff, sniff! The bear finds berries with its nose.
Say it with me. Bears have super noses!
Can you take a big sniff like a bear? Sniff, sniff, sniff!
Good sniffing!
Moo! Who is in the green meadow?
It is the cow!
Do all cows have the same nose?
No! Here is the fun fact. Every cow has its own nose print, just like your fingerprint.
No two cows have the same nose print. Just like you. There is only one you!
Say it with me. Every cow has its own nose!
Can you moo like a cow? Moooo!
What a lovely moo!
Wow! We met five friends with amazing noses. Now it is quiz time. Let's see what you remember!
Get ready. Think hard!
Whose nose is a long trunk? The elephant! Yes!
Whose horn is like your fingernails? The rhino! That's right!
Who digs with a snout? The pig! Good job!
Who has a super nose for berries? The bear! You remembered!
And who has a nose print like your fingerprint? The cow! You are so clever!
You learned five new things today. Elephant, rhino, pig, bear and cow.
Swing like an elephant. Stomp like a rhino. Oink like a pig. Sniff like a bear. And moo like a cow!
Now touch your own nose. Boop! Which nose was your favorite?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!

meta.title: Amazing Animal Noses for Kids! 5 Fun Facts with Milo

Sniff, sniff! Meet five animal friends with Milo the bluebird and learn one true fact about each nose: an elephant's trunk is its nose, a rhino's horn is made of the same stuff as your fingernails, pigs dig with their snouts, bears have a super sense of smell, and every cow has its own nose print.
A gentle animal lesson for kids with questions, actions to copy and a quiz at the end. Ages 2-6.
